title: Activation Functions
summary: Activation functions add nonlinearity to neural networks and affect gradient flow.

title: Actor-Critic
summary: Actor-critic methods train a policy actor and a value critic together.

title: Adam, AdamW, and Adagrad
summary: Adam, AdamW, and Adagrad adapt learning rates using gradient statistics.

title: AlphaGo
summary: AlphaGo combines policy networks, value networks, self-play, and Monte Carlo tree search for Go.

title: Autoencoders
summary: An autoencoder learns to compress input into a code and reconstruct it, which yields a useful representation.

title: Backpropagation
summary: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute gradients through a computation graph.

title: Bagging
summary: Bagging trains models on bootstrap resamples and averages them to cut variance.

title: BatchNorm, LayerNorm, and RMSNorm
summary: Normalization layers rescale activations to stabilize and speed neural network training.

title: Bayes' Theorem
summary: Bayes' theorem updates a prior belief with evidence to get a posterior belief.

title: Bellman Equations
summary: Bellman equations express value functions through immediate reward plus discounted future value.

title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
summary: Bias-variance tradeoff splits prediction error into systematic error, sample sensitivity, and noise.

title: Boosting
summary: Boosting fits weak learners in sequence, where each new learner corrects the errors of the current ensemble.

title: Causal Attention
summary: Causal attention masks future tokens so each position can only use past and current tokens.

title: Classifier-Free Guidance
summary: Classifier-free guidance combines conditional and unconditional denoising predictions to control generation.

title: Clustering Algorithms
summary: Clustering groups unlabeled points, with k-means, GMM, DBSCAN, hierarchical, and spectral as the main families.

title: Communication Primitives
summary: Communication primitives move tensors between ranks during distributed training.

title: Confidence Intervals
summary: A confidence interval gives a range of plausible parameter values from a sampling procedure.

title: Convex Functions
summary: Convex functions have no bad local minima and support strong optimization guarantees.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: CNNs use shared local filters to get translation equivariance and far fewer parameters than dense layers.

title: Credit Assignment Problem
summary: Credit assignment asks which past actions caused a later reward or loss.

title: Cross Attention
summary: Cross attention lets one sequence query information from another sequence.

title: Cross-Validation
summary: Cross-validation estimates generalization by training and validating across data splits.

title: Curriculum Learning
summary: Curriculum learning trains agents on tasks in a useful order, often from easier cases to harder cases.

title: Curse of Dimensionality
summary: In high dimensions volume grows fast, data becomes sparse, and distances between points concentrate.

title: Data Whitening
summary: Whitening transforms data so that features have zero mean, unit variance, and no correlation.

title: Decision Trees
summary: A decision tree splits the feature space with greedy axis aligned rules and predicts a constant in each leaf.

title: Decoding Techniques
summary: Decoding techniques choose output tokens from a language model probability distribution.

title: Determinant
summary: The determinant gives the signed volume scale of a square linear map.

title: Diffusion Forward and Reverse SDE
summary: Diffusion SDEs describe continuous-time noising and denoising through stochastic differential equations.

title: Diffusion Forward Process
summary: The diffusion forward process gradually corrupts data with Gaussian noise using a fixed Markov chain.

title: Diffusion Reverse Process
summary: The diffusion reverse process uses a learned denoiser to sample from noise back to data.

title: Dimensionality Reduction
summary: Methods that map high dimensional data to a lower dimensional space while keeping the structure that matters.

title: Direct Preference Optimization
summary: DPO trains a policy from preference pairs with a supervised loss derived from a KL-regularized reward objective.

title: Distributed Data Parallel
summary: DDP trains model replicas on different batch shards and synchronizes gradients across ranks.

title: Domain Adaptation
summary: Domain adaptation handles a shift between the training distribution and the deployment distribution.

title: Dot Product
summary: The dot product measures vector alignment and gives lengths, angles, and projections.

title: Dropout
summary: Dropout randomly removes activations during training to reduce co-adaptation and overfitting.

title: Early Stopping
summary: Early stopping ends training when validation performance stops improving.

title: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues
summary: Eigenvectors keep their direction under a matrix, and eigenvalues give the scale factor.

title: Ensembles
summary: Combining several models usually beats any single one, because errors partly cancel.

title: Entropy
summary: Entropy measures the average uncertainty or information content of a random variable.

title: Expectation
summary: The expectation is the weighted average value of a random variable.

title: Exploding and Vanishing Gradients
summary: Exploding and vanishing gradients occur when repeated Jacobian products grow or shrink too much.

title: Exploration vs Exploitation
summary: Exploration gathers information about actions. Exploitation uses current knowledge to get reward.

title: Few-Shot and Zero-Shot Learning
summary: Few-shot learning generalizes from a handful of examples per class, and zero-shot learning uses a shared semantic space instead of examples.

title: Finetuning
summary: Finetuning adapts a pretrained model to a task, domain, or response format.

title: Flash Attention
summary: FlashAttention computes exact attention with tiled kernels and much lower memory traffic.

title: Floating Point Representation
summary: Floating point numbers store sign, exponent, and significand bits with finite precision and range.

title: Flow Matching ODE
summary: Flow matching trains a vector field that transports a simple distribution to the data distribution.

title: Fully Sharded Data Parallel
summary: FSDP shards parameters, gradients, and optimizer state across data-parallel ranks.

title: GANs
summary: GANs train a generator and a discriminator in a two-player game to match a data distribution.

title: Generalization
summary: Generalization measures how well a model performs on new data from the target distribution.

title: Generalized Advantage Estimation
summary: GAE computes advantages by exponentially weighting multi-step TD errors.

title: Gradient Accumulation
summary: Gradient accumulation combines gradients from multiple microbatches before one optimizer step.

title: Gradient Checkpointing
summary: Gradient checkpointing saves activation memory by recomputing selected forward values during backward.

title: Gradient Clipping
summary: Gradient clipping limits gradient size to reduce unstable optimizer updates.

title: Gradient Descent and SGD
summary: Gradient descent updates parameters in the negative gradient direction to reduce loss.

title: Griffin
summary: Griffin is a hybrid sequence model that mixes recurrent gated layers with local attention.

title: Group Relative Policy Optimization
summary: GRPO normalizes rewards within groups of sampled responses and optimizes a clipped policy objective without a learned value critic.

title: Gumbel-Softmax
summary: The Gumbel-Softmax gives a differentiable relaxation of categorical sampling, so gradients pass through discrete choices.

title: Hessian
summary: The Hessian stores second partial derivatives and describes local curvature.

title: Imbalanced Data
summary: Imbalanced data has uneven class frequencies, which can make accuracy and training misleading.

title: Importance Sampling
summary: Importance sampling estimates expectations under one distribution with samples from another distribution.

title: Inverse of a Matrix
summary: A matrix inverse reverses a square linear map when the map has full rank.

title: Jacobian
summary: The Jacobian stores all first partial derivatives of a vector-valued function.

title: JAX, PyTorch, TensorFlow
summary: JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow are tensor frameworks with autodiff, accelerator support, and graph tools.

title: Jensen-Shannon Divergence
summary: Jensen-Shannon divergence is a symmetric, smoothed version of KL divergence.

title: JIT Compiling
summary: JIT compiling converts traced tensor programs into optimized execution plans at run time.

title: K-Nearest Neighbours
summary: k-NN predicts from the labels of the k closest training points, with no training phase and full memory cost.

title: KL Divergence
summary: KL divergence measures the expected log ratio between two probability distributions.

title: Linear Independence
summary: Linear independence means no vector in a set can be made from the others.

title: Linear Regression
summary: Linear regression fits a linear function by minimizing squared prediction error.

title: LLM Attention Scaling Factor
summary: The attention scaling factor divides dot products by the square root of the key dimension.

title: LLM vs RNN vs S4
summary: Transformers, RNNs, and S4 models use different ways to process sequence history.

title: LoRA
summary: LoRA adapts a frozen weight matrix with a small low-rank update.

title: Loss Functions
summary: A loss function maps predictions and targets to a scalar training objective.

title: Markov Decision Process
summary: An MDP models sequential decisions with states, actions, transitions, rewards, and a discount factor.

title: Markov Property
summary: The Markov property says the current state contains all information needed to predict the next state distribution.

title: Mixed Precision Training
summary: Mixed precision training uses lower-precision tensors for speed and memory while keeping key values stable.

title: Mixture of Experts
summary: Mixture of Experts uses a router to activate only a small subset of expert networks per token.

title: MLE vs MAP
summary: MLE maximizes likelihood, while MAP maximizes posterior probability with a prior.

title: Model-Based vs Model-Free
summary: Model-based RL learns or uses environment dynamics. Model-free RL learns policies or values without an explicit dynamics model.

title: Monte Carlo vs TD
summary: Monte Carlo methods use full returns. TD methods use bootstrapped one-step targets.

title: MuZero
summary: MuZero learns a latent dynamics model for planning without reconstructing observations.

title: Naive Bayes
summary: Naive Bayes applies Bayes' theorem with a conditional independence assumption over features.

title: Newton's Method
summary: Newton's method uses first and second derivatives to take curvature-aware optimization steps.

title: No Free Lunch Theorem
summary: Averaged over all possible problems, every learning algorithm has the same expected performance.

title: Null Space and Image Space
summary: The null space maps to zero, and the image space contains all outputs a matrix can produce.

title: Numerical Precision Tricks
summary: Numerical precision tricks make computations stable under finite floating point arithmetic.

title: On-Policy vs Off-Policy
summary: On-policy methods learn from data collected by the current policy. Off-policy methods can learn about one policy from another policy's data.

title: Orthogonality
summary: Orthogonality means vectors meet at a right angle and have zero dot product.

title: Overfitting and Underfitting
summary: Overfitting fits noise in training data, while underfitting misses real structure.

title: PDF and PMF
summary: PMFs assign probabilities to discrete values, while PDFs assign density to continuous values.

title: Perceiver
summary: Perceiver uses a latent bottleneck and cross attention to process large or multimodal inputs.

title: Pipeline Parallelism
summary: Pipeline parallelism splits model layers into stages and sends microbatches through the stages.

title: Policy Gradient Theorem
summary: The policy gradient theorem gives the gradient of expected return with respect to policy parameters.

title: Positive Semi-Definite
summary: A positive semi-definite matrix has nonnegative quadratic form values in all directions.

title: Precision, Recall, F1, and AUC-ROC
summary: Classification metrics built from the confusion matrix, and the curves that summarize behaviour across thresholds.

title: Pretraining
summary: Pretraining teaches a language model general patterns by optimizing a self-supervised objective on large text corpora.

title: Profiling
summary: Profiling measures time, memory, and hardware use so you can find training bottlenecks.

title: Proximal Policy Optimization
summary: PPO improves a policy with clipped probability ratios to limit destructive policy updates.

title: Q-Learning and TD Learning
summary: TD learning updates value estimates from bootstrapped one-step targets. Q-learning learns optimal action values off-policy.

title: Random Forests
summary: Random forests average many randomized decision trees to reduce variance.

title: Rank and Span
summary: Span is all reachable linear combinations, and rank is the dimension of that span.

title: Regularization Methods
summary: Regularization controls model complexity to reduce overfitting and improve generalization.

title: Relative Positional Embeddings
summary: Relative positional embeddings make attention depend on distances between tokens.

title: RLHF
summary: RLHF uses human preference data to train a reward model and optimize a language model.

title: RNNs and LSTMs
summary: Recurrent networks carry a hidden state across time, and gated cells such as the LSTM fix the vanishing gradient.

title: RoPE
summary: RoPE encodes positions by rotating query and key pairs before attention.

title: S4 and State Space Models
summary: S4 uses a linear state space recurrence with structured matrices, so it trains as a convolution and runs as an RNN.

title: SARSA
summary: SARSA is an on-policy TD control method that updates from the sampled state, action, reward, next state, and next action.

title: Scaling Laws
summary: Scaling laws describe how model loss changes with parameters, data, and compute.

title: Score Function
summary: The score function is the gradient of log density and gives the direction of increasing probability.

title: Second Order Methods
summary: Second order methods use curvature information to choose optimization steps.

title: Singular Matrices
summary: A singular matrix is a square matrix that has no inverse because it loses information.

title: Sinusoidal Embeddings
summary: Sinusoidal embeddings encode position with fixed sine and cosine waves at many frequencies.

title: Soft Actor-Critic
summary: Soft Actor-Critic maximizes reward and entropy with an off-policy actor-critic algorithm.

title: Support Vector Machines
summary: An SVM finds the separating hyperplane with the largest margin, and kernels extend it to nonlinear boundaries.

title: Tensor Parallelism
summary: Tensor parallelism splits large tensor operations across devices to reduce per-device memory and compute.

title: Tokenization
summary: Tokenization maps text to token IDs that a language model can process.

title: Transfer Learning
summary: Transfer learning reuses a model trained on a large source task to improve a smaller target task.

title: Transformer-XL
summary: Transformer-XL adds segment recurrence and relative positions to improve long-context modeling.

title: Unsupervised vs Supervised Learning
summary: Supervised learning fits input to label pairs, while unsupervised learning models structure in unlabeled data.

title: VAEs and VAE ELBO
summary: A VAE trains a latent-variable model with an evidence lower bound made from reconstruction and KL terms.

title: Variance and Covariance
summary: Variance measures spread, and covariance measures how two variables move together.

title: Variance Reduction in RL
summary: Variance reduction makes policy and value estimates more stable without changing the target when possible.

title: Weight Initialization
summary: Weight initialization sets starting parameter values to keep activations and gradients stable.

title: World Models and Dreamer
summary: World models learn latent dynamics so agents can train policies from imagined rollouts.
